ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory customer due diligence under Law No. 80 of 2002; screening of all shareholders, directors and UBOs against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, European Union Sanctions List, Egyptian terrorist designation list under Law No. 8 of 2015, and prohibited-party lists published by the Central Bank of Egypt and EMLCU. Enhanced due diligence applies to any Politically Exposed Person, including senior military officers, government procurement officials, heads of state and ministerial personnel. Source-of-wealth and source-of-funds must be documented for PEP and high-risk defense-sector transactions. Beneficial ownership must be traced through each corporate intermediate to identifiable natural persons where any interest at or above 25% exists, and persons conducting or significantly controlling the entity irrespective of legal possession must be declared.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) Investor Services Electronic Portal and the Commercial Registry of the Ministry of Trade and Industry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name of an Egyptian LLC must be in Arabic script. A Latin transliteration may be reserved for banking, invoicing and international trade use only if it faithfully corresponds to the registered Arabic name. The Arabic name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered trade name, trademark or protected corporate identifier in Egypt. Foreign words may be used in the Arabic name only after name-clearance review and must not violate Egyptian public order, military secrecy or defensive trade restrictions.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be renewed once for a further 30-day period by submitting a renewal request to GAFI before expiration. Upon rejection, the applicant may file a formal administrative grievance with the GAFI Complaints and Grievance Service within 15 days of the rejection notice, enclosing the rejection order, the proposed alternative names, and supporting documents. If the grievance is rejected or not answered within 15 working days, the applicant may file an administrative lawsuit before the competent Administrative Court in Cairo under Law No. 92 of 1970 and Law No. 9 of 2009. New name submissions may be refiled immediately through the portal after incorporating GAFI's stated grounds of refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted for this industry. ISIC 3040 manufacturing of armored security personnel transport vehicles is a defense-tactical business requiring physical industrial premises in Egypt, a registered lease or ownership title, and operational commercial substance satisfactory to GAFI and the military-licensing authorities. A virtual office may be used only for ancillary administrative correspondence and cannot singlehandedly satisfy the registered-office requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: approximately 75% probability of unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12 months of registration, given the temporary security nature of the military-grade vehicle production activity and the high AML/CFT risk rating.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 159 of 1981 (Egyptian Companies Law) as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; Executive Regulations of the Companies Law (Decree No. 96 of 1982). LLC provisions are governed by the Companies Law, Articles 38 et seq. and the GAFI executive rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), Ministry of Investment and Foreign Trade; Commercial Registry (Al-Sijill Al-Tijari)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association of the LLC (Aqd Al-Ta'sis wa Al-Nizam Al-Dakhili) in Arabic
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to LLCs under Law No. 159 of 1981. The subscribed capital is stated in the Memorandum of Association; the paid-up portion must be deposited in a bank account opened in the company's name, and the bank certificate must be attached to the incorporation application. Withdrawal of such capital is not permitted until incorporation is completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED FIRST: The subscription by the founding members to 1,000 ordinary shares, nominal value EGP 100 each, is approved, and the paid-up capital shall be deposited in the Company’s escrow account at a licensed Egyptian bank. RESOLVED SECOND: The registered office is fixed at Plot [__], Industrial Area, [__] Governorate, Arab Republic of Egypt. RESOLVED THIRD: [Name A] and [Name B] are appointed managers, with authority to execute incorporation documents, open bank accounts, and appear before GAFI, the Commercial Registry, the Industrial Development Authority, and the Ministry of Military Production. RESOLVED FOURTH: The managers are authorized to obtain tax cards, environmental approval, civil defense clearance, all operating licenses, and to sign and seal such applications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation and ISIC scope verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — One-Stop Shop, Ministry of Investment e-service portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File at least three proposed Arabic company names through the GAFI electronic registration portal, specifying the object of manufacturing armored security personnel transport vehicles under ISIC 3040. Verify that the selected name is not identical to any existing registered Egyptian company and does not contain restricted religious or political wording. Upon approval, obtain the official name reservation certificate.
required_dossiers: Completed GAFI name reservation application in Arabic
Certified passport copies and national IDs of all founding members
Notarized power of attorney if filing occurs through an agent
Corporate resolution and commercial extract if a founding member is a legal entity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, alternative names may be refiled within ten business days; a formal refusal may be appealed to the GAFI Complaints Committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and execution of the incorporation deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Notary Public Department, jointly with GAFI authentication officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Arabic Memorandum and Articles of Association containing the LLC name, object, authorized capital, share subscription schedule, managers, registered office, and duration. Execute the instrument before the Notary Public and obtain GAFI pre-certification where applicable. Ensure each founder's signature, legal capacity, and share allocation are attested in compliance with the Companies Law.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Name reservation certificate
Capital subscription schedule
Registered office lease or title evidence
Passport copies and notarized powers of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notarial queries are resolved by correcting the defective clauses and re-executing the instrument; foreign powers of attorney missing legalization may be cured by apostille or Egyptian consular legalization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital deposit and bank escrow certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank operating in Egypt
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a dedicated corporate account in the name of the LLC, deposit the paid-up capital from the founding members by wire transfer or cash, and obtain a bank certificate evidencing the deposit amount. The certificate must state the account holder, account number, and date of deposit, and must be attached to the GAFI incorporation file.
required_dossiers: Notarized draft incorporation instrument
Bank account opening application
Identity documents and beneficial ownership declaration of each founder
Source-of-funds documentation for the capital contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced AML/KYC information, submit a notarized beneficial ownership declaration and audited source-of-funds evidence; if the bank declines the account because of defense-sector risk, select a bank with a specialized compliance unit for military manufacturing clients.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Final GAFI registration and Commercial Registry issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the notarized incorporation deed, bank capital certificate, registered office lease, name reservation certificate, and completed GAFI forms. Pay the prescribed statutory fees and publication charges. GAFI will process the registration, register the LLC in the Commercial Registry, and issue the Certificate of Incorporation and preliminary taxpayer registration card.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Bank capital deposit certificate
Name reservation certificate
Registered office lease or title deed
GAFI application form and fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI suspends the application for incomplete documents, complete the file within fifteen days; an administrative refusal may be appealed to the GAFI internal dispute committee and thereafter to the administrative court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, social insurance, and municipal registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA); National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI); local municipal council
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the taxpayer card from GAFI or ETA, register all managers and employees with NOSI within the statutory period, and file the municipal license and signboard permit for the registered premises. If export operations are planned, complete exporter registration with the General Organization for Export and Import Control.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation
Tax registration form issued through GAFI
Manager and employee national IDs and photographs
Lease contract
Commercial Registry extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late NOSI filings are subject to statutory surcharges; rectification may be submitted to the NOSI office and penalty relief may be requested if the delay was caused by GAFI processing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA); Ministry of Military Production; Ministry of Defense Armament Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for an Industrial Operating License under Law No. 15 of 2017, attaching the production plan, facility layout, machinery register, and environmental approvals. For military tactical vehicles, obtain separate security authorization from the Ministry of Military Production and the Ministry of Defense, including background screening of managers, information security controls, and dual-use/export compliance. Commencement of production is prohibited until the industrial license and defense clearance are issued.
required_dossiers: Industrial license application (IDA Form)
Certificate of incorporation and Commercial Registry extract
Facility layout and manufacturing process description
Machinery purchase invoices or import documents
Environmental approval from the Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency
Security questionnaire and defense clearance application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IDA requests supplementary environmental, zoning, or technical data, cure the requirement through the Investment Services Center coordination desk; denial of defense clearance may be re-submitted after implementing the security conditions, and legal appeals follow Law No. 15 of 2017.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental impact assessment and civil defense clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA); Civil Defense Authority of the Ministry of Interior; Ministry of Manpower
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and obtain approval of a full environmental impact assessment for the armored-vehicle production facility, covering welding, painting, surface treatment, and hazardous waste storage. Install fire suppression systems and apply for the Civil Defense Fire Safety Certificate after site inspection. Obtain the occupational safety and health clearance from the Ministry of Manpower.
required_dossiers: Environmental impact assessment report
Industrial license application
Firefighting system installation certificates and test reports
Structural load inspection certificate from a licensed engineering firm
Workplace safety compliance checklist
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If EEAA imposes mitigation conditions, implement the environmental improvement plan and submit periodic monitoring reports; civil defense deficiencies are cured by retrofitting fire suppression equipment and scheduling re-inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) under the Ministry of Trade and Industry; Ministry of Military Production and Ministry of Defense for defense-related vehicle manufacture
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial Operating License (Al-Rokhsa Al-Sina'iyah) for Manufacture of Armored Security Personnel Transport Vehicles under Industrial Licensing Law No. 15 of 2017; Defense Industrial Security Clearance from the Ministry of Military Production

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) under Law No. 4 of 1994, as amended by Law No. 9 of 2009
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Full environmental impact assessment report required for factories performing metal fabrication, welding, painting, and surface treatment; EIA approval must be obtained before production commencement
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Ministerial Decree No. 402 of 2009 for wastewater discharges; Ministerial Decree No. 44 of 2000 for ambient air and stack emission limits; no untreated industrial effluent may be discharged to municipal sewers; VOC emissions shall be controlled through carbon filtration or thermal oxidation; hazardous wastes including paint sludge, solvents, and batteries shall be stored, manifested, and disposed in accordance with Law No. 4 of 1994 and Basel-compliant transfer requirements

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Fire Safety Certificate after inspection of fire water supply, hydrants, extinguishers, and gas suppression systems; structural load inspection certificate for high-bay vehicle assembly areas and roof-mounted equipment; Ministry of Manpower occupational safety clearance covering welding, painting, electrical, and mechanical safety; approved emergency evacuation and personal protective equipment programs

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance - Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA); e-Tax portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; e-Invoicing/e-Receipts portal: https://einvoice.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident or foreign-owned Egyptian LLC must obtain a unified Tax Identification Number (TIN) and VAT certificate before triggering taxable activities. Step 1: submit a unified registration application with certified articles of association, power of attorney, passport copies, and local premises/agent proof to the competent ETA tax office. Step 2: complete the unified tax registration form via the ETA e-Tax portal and receive the interim TIN. Step 3: register for VAT under Law 67/2016 when actual or expected annual taxable turnover exceeds EGP 500,000 or before the first import/supply; foreign entities not having a permanent establishment must appoint a fiscal representative for VAT. Step 4: request an e-signature certificate and activate the e-invoicing API account for clearance of taxable supply data.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Egyptian LLC under Law 159/1981 and Law 91/2005 is a separate legal taxpayer; corporate income tax is imposed on worldwide income of resident LLCs; no check-the-box or pass-through election is available in Egypt).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or analogous elective classification exists. Egyptian LLCs are mandatorily taxed as corporations. Specific statutory elections concern simplified VAT accounting for contractors (Article 20 VAT Law), installment payment procedures for customs duties, and optional allocation of head-office overhead by foreign branches under Article 30 of Law 91/2005. Hybrid mismatch elections are unavailable; treaty anti-abuse and BEPS Action 2 rules disallow deduction of hybrid mismatch payments.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) regulated under Egyptian Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended; ancillary stamp duty and table tax apply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover for mandatory registration; registration must be made per ETA procedures before the date the threshold is exceeded where future supplies make it reasonably determinable. Exporters of military hardware may be registered regardless of threshold for expedited clearance.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt mandates structured e-invoicing and e-receipting for all VAT-registered businesses. Sales invoices are issued as XML/JSON messages via ETA-certified REST APIs and must pass real-time schema validation from the ETA digital clearance platform. Cleared invoices receive a QR code and an ETA UUID; no manual paper invoices are permitted for B2B transactions between registered persons. Defense exporters must maintain digital signatures, PSD2-compliant APIs, and integrate with customs data systems. Submission deadline is generally at transaction time for real-time clearance and 72 hours for retroactive reconciliation of high-volume messages. Failure to clear an invoice may subject the seller to non-deductibility of input VAT and administrative penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating for exports is available under Law 67/2016 where the defense goods are physically exported from Egypt to a non-resident buyer within the statutory deadline, evidence of final customs exit is provided, and full foreign exchange proceeds are repatriated to Egypt through a licensed bank. Zero-rating also covers transferable defense services and ancillary transport, freight, and insurance directly attributable to the export. The Egyptian Customs Authority must confirm the goods left Egypt under a prior electronic export declaration; shipments to Free Zones are not eligible unless re-exported outside the country. A prior ETA no-objection letter should be obtained for military-tactical hardware subject to defense ministry approval.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (ECS) duly released by Egyptian Customs Authority
Electronic VAT export invoice with ETA clearance number and QR code
Bill of Lading, Airwaybill, or CMR international consignment note evidencing physical exit
Original commercial invoice and signed packing list
Foreign Currency Inward Remittance Certificate (from a licensed Egyptian bank) proving export proceeds repatriated within 180 days
Buyer's purchase order, diplomatic contract, or irrevocable letter of credit
Certificate of origin and defense-end-user certificate (when applicable)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA conducts post-clearance audits cross-referencing customs exit data, e-invoice clearance UUIDs, and bank foreign currency remittance records. Non-compliance or fictitious export schemes attract clawback of the zero rate (14% VAT becomes payable), an additional customs increment, fines ranging from EGP 20,000 to EGP 100,000 per invoice/declaration, and up to 200% of evaded tax as a risk-assessed penalty. If false declarations are intentional, criminal provisions may apply under the Customs Law and VAT Law, with imprisonment and disqualification of the fiscal representative. Non-repatriation of proceeds by day 180 automatically triggers de-zero-rating and suspension of future export privileges until full rectification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt maintains current account convertibility for bona fide trade and services, while capital account transactions remain subject to CBE authorisation and bank-level compliance review. Foreign investors may remit after-tax profits, dividends, and loan repayments under the unified investment framework, provided the company has filed all tax returns, obtained a tax clearance certificate, presented audited financial statements, and submitted the required CBE documentation through the servicing bank. Profit remittance is not automatically guaranteed; banks conduct source-of-funds verification and may impose sequencing or FX availability checks. The EGP operates under a managed float; all FX transactions must flow through CBE-authorised banks and be reported in the CBE Foreign Exchange Information and Monitoring System.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be repatriated to an Egyptian banking channel within four months from the date of shipment or such longer period as approved by the CBE. Exporters are permitted to retain export earnings in foreign currency accounts with authorised banks without a mandatory conversion into EGP; however, proceeds must be properly documented and reflected in the bank's foreign currency records. For defense and tactical hardware exporters, every inward receipt must carry a clear commercial invoice, customs export declaration, and end-user documentation, and any deviation from the statutory repatriation timeline must be reported to the CBE. There is no fixed percentage surrender ratio currently applicable, but the CBE can impose temporary directed conversion measures for macroprudential purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account / FX Settlement Account
Operational Account / Foreign Currency Account / LC Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMI platforms do not hold a CBE banking licence and cannot legally onboard an Egyptian LLC for capital injection, defense trade settlement, or FX clearing. Onshore fintech payment service providers may support collections or payroll, but they are not authorised to open documentary credit accounts, execute SWIFT MT103 cross-border payments, or provide CBE-compliant treasury clearing. All defense-related cross-border flows must pass through a CBE-licensed commercial bank with know-your-bank and sanctions screening infrastructure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one authorised signatory and the ultimate beneficial owner or a formally designated senior manager is typically mandatory for high-risk corporate accounts at tier-one Egyptian banks. The bank will conduct a KYC interview and a sanctions/PEP screening session. Remote opening may be possible only if all original documents are notarised and apostilled in the jurisdiction of the shareholders, a resident Egyptian manager holds an executed power of attorney, and the bank's compliance committee accepts a video-conference interview with signed procedural attestations. For defense-sector entities, CBE supervisory expectations strongly favour in-person attendance at a branch or head office.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and restricted-party screening mismatch against shareholders, directors, or counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete global sanctions screening report (UN, EU, OFAC, HMRC), no-hit output with methodology and screening date; a corporate chart with personal identification documents for each director and UBO; independent credit agency reports; a legal opinion from an international sanctions attorney; and a written compliance declaration signed by the CEO and MLRO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Defense nature of the company's products raising arms-trafficking or military end-use concern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid Egyptian defence production or manufacturing licence from the Ministry of Defence / Defence Industries Authority; end-user and end-use certificates; a copy of a sovereign procurement contract or official buyer's letter; government-issued export authorisation; factory inspection report; and a third-party compliance audit confirming compliance with arms-embargo and export-control laws.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in the ultimate beneficial ownership chain or nominee-shareholder arrangements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised registers of members and UBO declarations for all natural persons owning 25% or more; passports and proof of residential address; corporate formation certificates and board resolutions; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements; a group organisational chart; and an explanation of any trust or foundation layer with full trustee documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commercial purpose deviation for unusually large or unexplained FX flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of sales agreements, purchase orders, invoices, bills of lading, customs declarations, packing lists, inspection certificates, and audited financial statements; a cash-flow forecast supporting each projected transaction; and board minutes approving the treasury plan and delegated signatory matrix.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity contributions must be remitted via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's bank to the LLC's designated account at an authorised Egyptian bank. The payment must reference the CBE foreign direct investment purpose code for direct investment in Egyptian entities and include the company's corporate ID, the board resolution approving the capital increase or initial injection, and a certificate from the Egyptian General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) when applicable. The receiving bank will verify the source of wealth of the remitting shareholder, perform sanctions screening, and register the transaction in the CBE's external debt and FDI monitoring system. Any mismatch in the beneficiary name or purpose code may cause funds to be held pending compliance clearance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements flow through SWIFT MT103 for open-account payments and supplier advances, commercial letters of credit issued via SWIFT MT700/MT710 for procurement of military components, and standby LC/guarantees via MT760 for contract performance obligations. These rails require presentation of the commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading/airway bill, certificate of origin, inspection certificate, and, for military hardware, the original end-user certificate and export licence. Egyptian banks clear local-currency transfers through the CBE RTGS and electronic clearing system, while USD/foreign currency payments are routed through correspondent banks in New York, London, or Frankfurt, subject to correspondent bank compliance thresholds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable forwards with CBE-authorised banks for underlying trade exposures
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) entered through a licensed Egyptian bank or approved offshore counterparty under CBE circular guidance
Currency swaps for conversion of EGP and major foreign currencies, limited to trade-related and balance-sheet hedging
FX options traded on an OTC basis with CBE-licensed banks, exercisable against demonstrated commercial exposures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers, no later than 30 April of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of EGP 5,000–20,000; monthly late-payment interest of 2% on unpaid tax; prolonged non-filing may trigger administrative license suspension and criminal enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Financial Statements and Annual General Assembly Minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the fiscal year-end; Calendar-year entities must file by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of up to EGP 20,000 per infraction under Companies Law No. 159/1981, plus EGP 1,000 for each additional month; repeated omission may lead to administrative strike-off and loss of legal status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) Confirmation Statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing due within 15 days following the ordinary general assembly; before 1 March for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine from EGP 10,000 to EGP 30,000 under AML Law No. 80/2002; non-compliance may block access to public banks and government tenders.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade and Industry – Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the registration anniversary date of the company’s commercial license
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment surcharge of 2% per month; failure to renew for 12 months may result in administrative removal from the commercial registry.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Every Egyptian LLC must appoint at least one Certified Public Accountant (CPA) auditor, irrespective of size. A mandatory independent audit is triggered when paid-in capital exceeds EGP 500,000, annual turnover exceeds EGP 10,000,000, the company is engaged in defense-related contracts, or the Tax Authority imposes audited certification requirements under Income Tax Law No. 91/2005.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), which largely align with IFRS; publicly-interest entities and defense contractors may be required by GAFI to adopt full IFRS. Military-adjacent manufacturers must maintain cost-accounting records compliant with Ministry of Defense audit protocols.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under GAFI/AML Cabinet Decree No. 44/2020, every LLC must identify any individual or entity holding direct or indirect ownership of at least 25% of shares or voting rights. The UBO register must be updated within 15 days of any share transfer or ownership change, and an annual confirmation must be submitted to GAFI verifying the completeness and accuracy of the register for the prior calendar year.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $250–$900 per year for a registered office/agent in Cairo, including GAFI representation and annual retainer
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $1,500–$4,000 for a certified audit of a mid-sized manufacturing LLC holding defense-related licenses

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Flat 22.5% rate for commercial and industrial companies under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005; no automatic statutory tax holiday for an LLC. Applicable reliefs: (i) investment-cost deduction of 30%-50% of invested capital for licensed strategic projects under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, subject to ministerial approval and issuance of an investment certificate; (ii) Free Zone company regime at 0% CIT on export-related profits where a Free Zone license is held and the statutory annual fee is paid; (iii) accelerated depreciation deductions for qualifying industrial machinery and equipment; (iv) unilateral and treaty foreign tax credit relief on foreign-source income. Defence-tactical manufacturing under ISIC 3040 requires separate clearance by the Ministry of Defence / Ministry of Military Production but confers no additional tax exemption.
